headline: On the bleeding edge, always learning.
lede: The 2021 version of this site said “I love to learn new technologies.” Still true. The difference now is that iteration is orders of magnitude faster, so attention to detail matters more than ever: when anything can ship in minutes, the details are the work.

items.how: By running one for real instead of reading about it: chkm8, on a custom agent harness, with its own accounts and its own wallet.
On a live cluster, not a tutorial: GitOps deploys, CronJobs and a position monitor that has to stay up.
With real money at small size on [Lighter](https://lighter.xyz). Margin, leverage and stops explained in plain language with simple examples first, then a backtest, then a trade.
Many agents splitting one job. Reading [Swarms](https://www.swarms.ai/) and testing where a crowd of agents beats one good one.
Agents that pay for their own API calls over plain HTTP, in stablecoins, with no accounts or API keys: [x402](https://x402.org/).
Spending limits enforced on-chain with [EIP-7702](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-7702) session keys, not only in chkm8's scripts: a daily budget and a short list of contracts it may touch.
On-chain identity and reputation for agents ([ERC-8004](https://eips.ethereum.org/EIPS/eip-8004), still a draft), so one agent can check another before paying it.
Measuring whether an agent is getting better or worse over time. Service-level targets, but for agents.
Packaging chkm8's tools as [MCP](https://modelcontextprotocol.io/) servers that other agents can call, and eventually pay for over x402.
